page: Microsoft Azure F8as_v7 belongs to the Fasv7 compute-optimized virtual machine family, built on x86_64 AMD processors and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory, equating to an allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server is strictly a CPU-driven instance and includes no graphics processing units.

Storage configuration on the F8as_v7 relies entirely on external volumes, as the instance features no bundled local disk capacity. It is designed to interface with Premium Storage for durable read and write operations. In addition, the virtual machine is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on private networking or separately configured address resources.

The absence of local disks minimizes storage overhead for stateless architectures or nodes using dedicated remote persistent disks. Provisioning 4.0 GB of memory per core provides adequate headroom for compute-focused tasks without over-allocating system memory. This profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for consistent, dedicated thread execution. Recommended workloads include web serving, application middleware, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure F8as_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by AMD processor hardware, the instance is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a resource ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance architecture does not bundle integrated local storage, instead utilizing external Premium Storage connectivity for operating system and data volumes. Furthermore, the F8as_v7 includes zero GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating purely on network-attached infrastructure. By offering dedicated CPU resources without local drive overhead, this configuration delivers predictable execution for core-driven tasks that prioritize external storage durability over ephemeral scratch space. Recommended workload fits include web servers, batch processing jobs, build and continuous integration environments, enterprise microservices, and compute workloads requiring consistent multithreaded capacity.
